name: A roof from stairs
about: Rows of stairs that step up to the middle.

steps.title: Walls first
steps.say: Build four walls, two blocks high. Logs at the corners make it look strong.
steps.tip: Leave a gap in the front wall for a door.

steps.title: Stairs along the long sides
steps.say: Put a row of stairs along the front and the back, one block out past the walls. Fill the top of the walls with planks.
steps.tip: Stand outside, facing the wall, as you place each stair. The low side faces you, so the tall side points to the middle.

steps.title: Up one and in one
steps.say: Put the next row of stairs on top of the planks, one block in from the last row. Fill the middle with planks again.
steps.tip: Each row sits one block higher and one block further in. That makes the slope.

steps.title: Close the top
steps.say: The last two rows of stairs meet in the middle, back to back. That's the top of your roof.
steps.tip: A roof in a darker wood than the walls stands out. Try spruce or dark oak.

name: Walls with depth
about: Logs, trim and a deep window.

steps.title: A wall with a deep window
steps.say: Build a flat wall with a hole for a window. Put the glass one block further in, not in line with the wall.
steps.tip: A deep window makes a wall look thick and strong.

steps.title: Logs that stick out
steps.say: Put a column of logs at each end, one block out in front of the wall.
steps.tip: On a long wall, add a column of logs every 4 or 5 blocks.

steps.title: Upside-down stairs
steps.say: Put upside-down stairs along the top, between the logs. Put three more under the window, as a ledge.
steps.tip: To place a stair upside down, point at the top half of the block's side.

steps.title: A stone bottom row
steps.say: Swap the bottom row of planks for stone bricks. It gives the wall a strong base.
steps.tip: Two or three kinds of block in one wall look better than one.

steps.title: A window
steps.say: Make a hole in the wall and fill it with glass. This one is 3 wide and 2 high.
steps.tip: Glass panes are thinner than glass blocks, so the window looks set into the wall.

steps.title: Shutters
steps.say: Put trapdoors on the wall on each side of the window, two high. Open them, and they look like shutters.
steps.tip: A trapdoor sticks to the block you point at. Tap it to open or shut it.

steps.title: A ledge under it
steps.say: Put trapdoors under the window and leave them shut. Point high on the wall, so they sit at the top of the space.
steps.tip: Point at the top half of a block's side, and the trapdoor goes at the top.

steps.title: A little roof
steps.say: Put a row of stairs above the window, against the wall, like a little roof.
steps.tip: Use the same wood for the shutters and the roof, so they go together.

name: Doors and porches
about: A step up and a little roof.

steps.title: A door one block up
steps.say: Build the wall on a row of stone, so the door sits one block up.
steps.tip: Doors are two blocks tall. An iron door needs a button or a lever to open it.

steps.title: A step
steps.say: Put a stair in front of the door, as a step. The low side goes away from the door.
steps.tip: Stand in front of the door to place it. The low side of a stair always faces you.

steps.title: Posts and a roof
steps.say: Put two fence posts out front, two high, with a row of slabs on top. Now it's a porch.
steps.tip: Use the same wood for the door, the posts and the roof, so it all goes together.

name: Paths that look real
about: Wiggly, mixed and full of flowers.

steps.title: A wiggly path
steps.say: Use a shovel on grass to make a dirt path. Let it wiggle a little, and make it wider in places.
steps.tip: A shovel turns grass or dirt into a dirt path. Straight paths look less natural.

steps.title: Mix it up
steps.say: Swap some path blocks for gravel and coarse dirt. Put them here and there, not in a pattern.
steps.tip: Messy edges make a path look like people have walked on it for years.

steps.title: Flowers along the sides
steps.say: Put flowers and ferns along the sides of the path. Leave some gaps.
steps.tip: Bone meal on grass grows grass and flowers around it.

name: Your own trees
about: Bigger and rounder than real ones.

steps.title: A trunk with roots
steps.say: Stack logs five high for the trunk. Put one more log on each side at the bottom, like roots.
steps.tip: A tree you build can be any shape you like.

steps.title: A ball of leaves
steps.say: Put leaves all around the top of the trunk. Make it round, but miss out a few corners.
steps.tip: Leaves you place yourself never fall off, even far from a log.

steps.title: Leaves hanging down
steps.say: Add a few single leaves hanging under the edges. It makes the tree look soft.
steps.tip: Use shears to pick up leaves. Without shears, you only get a sapling or a stick now and then.

name: Fences and gates
about: A pen with posts and a gate.

steps.title: A ring of fence
steps.say: Put fence all the way round. Fences join up to each other by themselves.
steps.tip: Animals can't jump over a fence, so it keeps them in.

steps.title: A gate
steps.say: Swap one fence for a fence gate, so you can get in and out.
steps.tip: Tap the gate to open it. Shut it behind you!

steps.title: Posts at the corners
steps.say: Swap the corner fences for logs, and put a lantern on each.
steps.tip: Light keeps monsters from spawning inside the pen.

name: Flower boxes
about: Trapdoors round a strip of grass.

steps.title: Grass under the window
steps.say: Put a row of grass or dirt under a window, one block out from the wall.
steps.tip: A Silk Touch tool picks up grass blocks. Or just use dirt.

steps.title: Box it in
steps.say: Put open trapdoors on the front and the ends of the grass, so it looks like a box.
steps.tip: Point at the side of the grass to place each trapdoor, then tap it to open it.

steps.title: Plant flowers
steps.say: Plant flowers in the box. Mix two or three colours.
steps.tip: Try leaves instead of flowers to make a little hedge.

steps.title: A plain floor
steps.say: Rooms get dark without lights. Here's a plain wooden floor.
steps.tip: Torches work, but lots of them on the walls can look messy.

steps.title: A light in the floor
steps.say: Break one floor block in the middle and put glowstone in its place.
steps.tip: Sea lanterns and shroomlights work too.

steps.title: Carpet on top
steps.say: Put carpet over the glowstone and around it. The light still shines up through the carpet.
steps.tip: Carpet doesn't block light, so the room is bright and you can't see the lamp.

name: Small details
about: A bench, a lamp and a plant.

steps.title: A plain wall
steps.say: Start with a plain wall. Small things in front of it make it feel lived in.
steps.tip: Look at real houses for ideas: benches, lamps, plants and boxes.

steps.title: A bench
steps.say: Put two stairs against the wall for a seat. Open trapdoors on each end make the arms.
steps.tip: Open trapdoors stand up flat, so they make good arms, shutters and little fences.

steps.title: A lamp post
steps.say: A fence post with a lantern on top makes a little street lamp.
steps.tip: A lantern can sit on top of a block, or hang under one.

steps.title: A barrel and a plant
steps.say: Put a barrel by the wall, with a flower pot on top. Put a flower in the pot.
steps.tip: A barrel holds as much as a chest, so a detail can be useful too.
